title: PyTorch CUDA out of memory

parts: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB while fine-tuning a 7B model on my laptop GPU.

Reduce memory in this order: lower the batch size to 1 and use gradient accumulation, enable gradient checkpointing, load the model in 4-bit with bitsandbytes (QLoRA), and shorten max sequence length.
I only have 8 GB VRAM. Will QLoRA fit a 7B model?
Often yes with 4-bit weights, LoRA rank 8-16, batch size 1 and a sequence length around 512. Expect slow training. A 3B model is more comfortable at 8 GB.

title: Poetry dependency management and lockfile

parts: hey im confused between poetry and pipenv for my new python backend service. which one handles lockfiles better?

Poetry is generally preferred today over Pipenv for several reasons:
1. Lockfile resolution in Poetry uses an exact SAT solver (resolvelib-like algorithm) which is much faster and deterministic.
2. Poetry adheres strictly to PEP 517/518 pyproject.toml standards.
3. Pipenv historically had very slow locking issues on large dependency trees.
wait what is the command in poetry to add a dev dependency like pytest

In modern Poetry (v1.2+), use dependency groups:
```bash
poetry add pytest --group dev
```
In older versions it was `poetry add -D pytest`, but groups are the standard now.
how does poetry export to requirements.txt for docker build

You use the poetry export plugin:
```bash
poetry export --without-hashes --format=requirements.txt > requirements.txt
```
You can also add `--without dev` to only export production dependencies.
wait why without-hashes? isn't hashes safer?

Hashes are safer for security, but pip install inside Docker often fails if platform wheels differ or if hashes for git/editable dependencies are missing. If you build linux wheels on mac, hashes might mismatch.
can poetry resolve private pypi repositories?

Yes! You configure a secondary repository with:
```bash
poetry source add --priority=supplemental my-repo https://pypi.company.com/simple/
poetry config http-basic.my-repo username password
```
what if two dependencies need different versions of urllib3?

Poetry will fail fast with a SolverProblemError displaying the exact version conflict tree. Unlike pip which might silently overwrite or backtrack indefinitely, Poetry forces you to resolve the constraint.
is there a poetry show command to inspect the tree?
Yes, run `poetry show --tree`. It prints the entire hierarchical dependency tree with active and requested versions.
how to update only one package without updating everything?
Run `poetry update requests`. That updates only `requests` and its sub-dependencies, preserving the lockfile for all other packages.
what about poetry run vs poetry shell?
`poetry run <cmd>` executes a command directly in the virtualenv without altering your current terminal environment. `poetry shell` spawns a subshell with the virtualenv activated.
does poetry build create both sdist and wheel?
Yes, running `poetry build` outputs both a source distribution (`.tar.gz`) and a binary wheel (`.whl`) inside the `dist/` directory.
awesome, this completely clarifies poetry lockfile resolution and workflow thanks!
You're welcome! Poetry's deterministic lockfile and pyproject.toml workflow make it a great choice for production python services.

title: PyTorch device selection cuda vs mps

parts: how to write a universal device check in pytorch for cuda vs apple silicon mps vs cpu?

Use this standard pattern:
```python
import torch

if torch.cuda.is_available():
    device = torch.device('cuda')
elif torch.backends.mps.is_available():
    device = torch.device('mps')
else:
    device = torch.device('cpu')
print(f'Using device: {device}')
```
does mps support all torch operations like complex numbers or scatter?

Most common operations are supported, but some specialized ops (e.g. certain 3D convolutions, complex fft, or double precision float64) may fall back to CPU or raise `NotImplementedError`. You can set `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1` in your environment to automatically fall back to CPU for unsupported ops.

title: PyTorch mixed precision fp16 vs bf16

parts: whats the difference between fp16 and bf16 in pytorch amp autocast?

The key difference is exponent vs mantissa bits:
- `fp16`: 1 sign, 5 exponent, 10 mantissa bits. High precision but narrow dynamic range (max ~65504). Prone to underflow/overflow, requiring `GradScaler`.
- `bf16`: 1 sign, 8 exponent, 7 mantissa bits. Same dynamic range as fp32 (8 exponent bits), but lower precision. It rarely underflows or overflows, so no GradScaler is needed.
Use `torch.bfloat16` if your GPU supports it (NVIDIA Ampere A100/RTX 30xx or newer).
do I still use torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler with bf16?
No! With `torch.autocast(device_type='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)`, `GradScaler` is unnecessary and should be omitted because bf16 doesn't suffer from gradient underflow.

title: Qdrant compound payload filtering

parts: how do i do compound filtering in qdrant with both must and should conditions in python

Use `models.Filter` from `qdrant_client.http`:
```python
from qdrant_client.http import models

query_filter = models.Filter(
    must=[
        models.FieldCondition(key="user_id", match=models.MatchValue(value="usr_123")),
        models.FieldCondition(key="status", match=models.MatchValue(value="active")),
    ],
    should=[
        models.FieldCondition(key="category", match=models.MatchValue(value="ai")),
        models.FieldCondition(key="category", match=models.MatchValue(value="python")),
    ]
)
client.search(collection_name="docs", query_vector=vec, query_filter=query_filter)
```
does qdrant support range filtering on numeric timestamps?

Yes, use `models.Range`:
```python
models.FieldCondition(key="created_at", range=models.Range(gte=1672531200, lte=1704067200))
```
Make sure to create a payload index on `created_at` with `schema=models.PayloadSchemaType.INTEGER` for fast lookups.

title: Cross-encoder reranking with BAAI bge-reranker

parts: why should i use a cross-encoder to rerank after rrf fusion in rag?

Bi-encoders (like vector embeddings) compute query and document representations independently in vector space. While very fast for first-stage candidate retrieval, they miss token-level cross-attention interactions.
A cross-encoder passes the query and document together into the transformer layers simultaneously (`[CLS] query [SEP] document [SEP]`), allowing full self-attention across every word pair. This provides drastically superior relevance scoring.
which cross-encoder model is recommended for general text search?
`BAAI/bge-reranker-base` or `BAAI/bge-reranker-large` are currently state of the art open weights models. `bge-reranker-base` runs fast on CPU or small GPUs with sentence-transformers.
how do i load and predict with BAAI/bge-reranker-base in python?

```python
from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder

model = CrossEncoder('BAAI/bge-reranker-base')
pairs = [[query, doc_text] for doc_text in candidates]
scores = model.predict(pairs, batch_size=32)
```
are the scores raw logits or probabilities?

By default, `model.predict(pairs)` returns raw unnormalized logits (which can range from negative numbers like -8.0 up to positive +8.0). If you need scores bounded in [0, 1], apply `scipy.special.expit(scores)` (sigmoid) or pass `apply_softmax=True` if supported.
how many candidates should i pass into reranking?
Typically 20 to 50 candidates from first-stage retrieval. Passing 100+ candidates adds excessive latency since cross-encoders are $O(N)$ transformer inferences per query.
what latency should i expect on cpu vs gpu for 30 candidates?
On an modern 8-core CPU, scoring 30 candidates with bge-reranker-base takes ~150-300ms. On an NVIDIA GPU (T4 or A10), it takes ~15-25ms.
can a cross-encoder score be used for relevance gating?

Yes! Because cross-encoder scores measure true semantic relevance rather than relative rank, setting a minimum score threshold (like sigmoid score >= 0.35 or logit >= -2.0) is very effective at filtering out irrelevant noise.
should query and doc be truncated if too long?
Yes, `CrossEncoder(..., max_length=512)`. Excessively long documents will be truncated; in RAG, you want each candidate chunk to be around 200-400 tokens.
does bge-reranker support multilingual text?
Yes, `bge-reranker-base` and `bge-reranker-large` support both English and Chinese, with solid performance across other major languages.
awesome, this covers the cross-encoder reranker architecture completely.
Glad to help! A hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval pipeline with RRF followed by a BGE cross-encoder reranker is industry standard.

title: Polars LazyFrame query optimization and posture

parts: how does polars lazyframe optimize queries compared to eager dataframe?

When using `pl.scan_parquet()` or `df.lazy()`, Polars builds a logical query plan without executing immediately. The query optimizer applies:
1. Predicate pushdown: filters (`.filter()`) are evaluated at the storage level, skipping unneeded parquet row groups.
2. Projection pushdown: only referenced columns (`.select()`) are loaded into RAM.
3. Common subplan elimination and slice pushdown.
Call `.collect()` to execute the optimized plan.

title: Pydantic v2 migration and validators

parts: I'm migrating a FastAPI codebase from Pydantic v1 to Pydantic v2. What replaced @validator and @root_validator?

In Pydantic v2:
- `@validator` is replaced by `@field_validator('field_name', mode='before'|'after')`.
- `@root_validator` is replaced by `@model_validator(mode='before'|'after')`.
Also, `mode='after'` validators receive the validated model instance `self` directly in model_validator, whereas `mode='before'` validators receive the raw dictionary `data` before field validation.
How do I forbid extra fields in a Pydantic v2 model?

Instead of the old `class Config:` inner class, use `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')`:
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

class MyModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    name: str
    age: int
```
What happened to .dict() and .json()?

They are deprecated and will be removed in v3. Use:
- `model.model_dump()` instead of `.dict()`
- `model.model_dump_json()` instead of `.json()`
What replaced parse_obj()?
Use `MyModel.model_validate(obj)` instead of `MyModel.parse_obj(obj)`. For JSON strings, use `MyModel.model_validate_json(raw_json)`.
Can you show an example of @model_validator(mode='after') checking cross-field constraints?
What about schema() for OpenAPI generation?
Use `MyModel.model_json_schema()` instead of `MyModel.schema()`.
Is Pydantic v2 much faster because of pydantic-core?
Yes, pydantic-core is written in Rust. Parsing and validation benchmarks typically show 5x to 20x speedups compared to v1 pure Python implementation.
Does Field(..., regex=...) still work?
No, `regex` was renamed to `pattern`, e.g. `Field(pattern=r'^[a-z]+$')`.
What about custom types with __get_validators__?
Custom types now use `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` from `pydantic_core.core_schema` or `Annotated[T, BeforeValidator(...)]`.
This covers all the breaking changes I was hitting, thanks!
Glad to help! The v1 to v2 migration is straightforward once you know the new `model_dump`, `ConfigDict`, and validator conventions.

title: FastAPI JWT Bearer auth header

parts: how to extract and verify a Bearer JWT in a fastapi header dependency?

Use `HTTPBearer` from `fastapi.security` and `jwt.decode` from PyJWT:
```python
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPBearer, HTTPAuthorizationCredentials
import jwt

security = HTTPBearer()

def get_current_user(creds: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials = Depends(security)):
    token = creds.credentials
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(token, 'SECRET_KEY', algorithms=['HS256'])
        return payload['sub']
    except jwt.PyJWTError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail='Invalid token')
```

title: Git stash pop vs apply

parts: whats the difference between git stash pop and git stash apply?

title: Sourdough bread bulk fermentation troubleshooting

parts: my sourdough loaf came out dense and flat with gummy crumb. what went wrong?

Dense, flat sourdough with a gummy crumb usually points to one of three issues:
1. Under-fermentation (bulk fermentation didn't build enough gas volume).
2. Weak gluten development (dough couldn't hold its shape during bake).
3. Slicing while still warm (steam condenses inside, causing gumminess). What was your hydration percentage and bulk time?
i used 75% hydration and bulk fermented for 3 hours at 21 celsius.

At 21°C (70°F), 3 hours is definitely under-fermented! Sourdough fermentation at room temp 21°C typically needs 5 to 7 hours until the dough rises 50-75%, becomes domed with rounded edges, and shows bubbles underneath.
how many stretch and folds do you do during bulk?
4 sets of stretch and folds spaced 30 minutes apart during the first 2 hours of bulk fermentation. After the 4th set, let the dough rest undisturbed for the remainder of bulk.
should the first set be coil folds or stretch and fold?
Start with stretch and folds for the first 2 sets when the dough is stiffer, then switch to gentle coil folds for sets 3 and 4 as gluten develops and gas accumulates to avoid knocking air out.
how do i know when bulk fermentation is done?

Don't watch the clock; watch the dough. Look for:
- 50-75% rise in volume.
- Top surface is smooth and domed with a few translucent bubbles.
- Jiggly when you gently shake the bowl.
- The poke test: gentle indentation slowly springs back halfway.
what temperature for Dutch oven baking?

Preheat Dutch oven at 230°C (450°F) for 45-60 minutes. Bake covered with lid for 20 minutes (steam enables oven spring), then remove lid and bake uncovered at 220°C (425°F) for 20-25 minutes until deep mahogany crust forms.
do i need ice cubes inside the dutch oven for steam?
A single ice cube dropped between the parchment paper and Dutch oven wall creates a burst of steam that improves blistered crust and blister ear, though not strictly required if the lid fits tightly.
how long to wait before slicing the loaf?
Wait at least 2 hours, ideally until the loaf reaches room temperature (around 25°C). The interior starches are still setting as it cools.
what flour mix do you recommend for beginners?
80% unbleached strong bread flour (12.5-13% protein) and 20% whole wheat flour. The whole wheat speeds up microbial activity while bread flour gives strong gluten structure.
this explains why my loaf was flat, my kitchen was way too cold for a 3 hour bulk. thanks!

title: Pizza dough cold fermentation and career switch

parts: why does 72 hour cold fermentation make pizza dough taste so much better?

At refrigerator temperatures (3-4°C), yeast activity slows down dramatically while enzymatic activity continues. Enzymes (amylases and proteases) break complex starches into simple sugars and proteins into amino acids. This creates:
1. Complex rich flavor (organic acids and esters).
2. Superior browning and leopard spotting from caramelized simple sugars.
3. Tender, easily digestible gluten structure.

2. Learn git, testing, and debugging deeply—juniors who can debug and write clean tests stand out immediately.
3. Leverage your unique story: teamwork in fast-paced high-pressure environments translates directly to tech teams.

how should i divide Tokyo neighborhoods across 5 days?

Early morning before 7:30 AM! Nakamise street shops won't be open yet, but the temple grounds are tranquil and magical without tourist crowds. Alternatively, visit at 9:00 PM when the pagoda is illuminated.
how does mobile internet work? esim vs pocket wifi?

where can i get great ramen without waiting 2 hours in line?

parts: how much budget do i need for 7 days in Vietnam doing Hanoi and Da Nang?

nice. trying to pack everything in a 7kg carry-on reminds me of the 0/1 knapsack algorithm in CS! how does dynamic programming solve that again?

Haha, exact match! In 0/1 Knapsack:
Let `dp[i][w]` be the maximum value possible using a subset of the first `i` items with max weight capacity `w`.
For item `i` with weight `wt` and value `val`:
- If `wt > w`: `dp[i][w] = dp[i-1][w]` (can't take it).
- Else: `dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], val + dp[i-1][w - wt])`.
You fill a 2D table in $O(N \times W)$ time and space, or optimize space to 1D array iterating weight backwards.

title: System design interview preparation roadmap

parts: what is a comprehensive preparation roadmap for senior backend system design interviews?

Follow a 4-step structured roadmap over 4 to 8 weeks:
1. Foundations: Networking (TCP/HTTP/gRPC), Caching (Redis/Memcached, Cache-Aside vs Write-Through), Database scaling (Replication, Sharding, B-Tree vs LSM), and Message queues (Kafka/RabbitMQ).
2. Core trade-offs: CAP theorem, PACELC, strong consistency vs eventual consistency.
3. Standard design patterns: Rate limiters, URL shorteners, distributed ID generation (Snowflake), notification systems, chat apps.
4. Mock interviews with real-time feedback.
how should i pace the 45-minute interview?

Divide into 4 distinct phases:
- 0-5 mins: Clarify requirements & scope (functional, non-functional, latency, QPS, data retention).
- 5-10 mins: High-level design (draw key services, DB, cache, load balancers).
- 10-30 mins: Deep dive into core bottlenecks, data schema, APIs, and scaling.
- 30-40 mins: Failure modes, resiliency, monitoring, and single points of failure.
- 40-45 mins: Wrap up and interview questions.
how to calculate QPS and storage estimations?

Memorize quick powers of 10:
- 1 million requests/day $\approx$ 12 requests/second ($10^6 / 86400$).
- 100 million daily active users $\approx$ 1,200 QPS average, ~2,400 peak.
- Storage: 100 million posts/day $\times$ 500 bytes = 50 GB/day $\approx$ 18 TB/year.
what is the best approach for unique ID generation without single point of failure?

Twitter Snowflake approach: 64-bit integer consisting of:
- 1 sign bit (0)
- 41 bits timestamp in milliseconds (~69 years)
- 10 bits worker / machine node ID (1024 nodes)
- 12 bits sequence number (4096 IDs per millisecond per node).
Provides k-sortable, decentralized, high-throughput unique IDs without database coordination.
SQL vs NoSQL: how do I justify my choice in the interview?

Justify by access patterns and consistency needs:
- Choose SQL (PostgreSQL, MySQL) when: ACID transactions are required (financial transactions), data has relational foreign keys, schema is stable, and complex JOINs are common.
- Choose NoSQL (Cassandra, DynamoDB, MongoDB) when: massive write volume requiring horizontal partitioning, flexible schema, key-value or document lookups by partition key, and eventual consistency is acceptable.
how to handle hot partition keys in sharded databases?

Add a salt or suffix to hot keys (e.g. `celebrity_user_id_#` where `#` is 0-9) to spread writes across 10 shards, and query shards in parallel with scatter-gather during reads. Or use an aggressive Redis cache in front of read-heavy partitions.
what is circuit breaker pattern?

title: Couch to 5k running and shin splints prevention

parts: started couch to 5k week 2 and my shins hurt when running. how to prevent shin splints?

Shin splints (medial tibial stress syndrome) are common beginner overuse injuries. How to fix:
1. Shorten your stride: avoid overstriding (landing with heel far out in front of your knee). Land with feet directly underneath your hips.
2. Increase cadence to ~160-170 steps per minute.
3. Run on softer surfaces (dirt path or asphalt instead of concrete sidewalks).
4. Strengthen tibialis anterior with heel walks and toe raises.
5. If pain is sharp and hurts when walking, rest 3-5 days to avoid a stress fracture.

title: Minor pentatonic box 1 blues solo phrasing

parts: i learned the A minor pentatonic box 1 on guitar (frets 5 and 8). how do i make it sound like music instead of just running scales up and down?

Running scales up and down sounds like an exercise. To make it sound like real blues/rock solos:
1. Phrasing and breathing: play a short 3-note idea, then pause for 2 beats like a singer taking a breath.
2. Use articulation: string bending, vibrato, hammer-ons, and slides.

which note should i bend in box 1?
The money bend in A minor pentatonic box 1 is the 7th fret on the G string (D note) bent up a whole step to E! Also bend the 8th fret on the B string (G note) bent a whole step to A.
how do i do vibrato without throwing my finger off the string?
Rotate your forearm and wrist like turning a doorknob, rather than wiggling just your finger joint. Keep the finger anchored and pivot from the wrist.
what is the 'blues note' added to pentatonic?
The flat 5th ($b5$). In A minor, that's the D# / Eb note at the 8th fret on the A string or the 8th fret on the G string. Passing through this note creates the classic grit of the Blues Scale.
can i use the same box 1 shape for other keys?
Yes! The pattern is movable. Move your index finger to the 3rd fret for G minor, 7th fret for B minor, 10th fret for D minor, and 12th fret for E minor.
what is a call and response pattern in soloing?
Play a short musical phrase (the 'call'), then answer it with a resolving phrase (the 'response'), like a conversation between two instruments.
how to stop adjacent strings from ringing out during bends?
Mute with both hands: use the palm of your picking hand to rest against lower pitch strings, and let the index finger of your fretting hand gently touch adjacent strings.
should i practice with a metronome or backing tracks?
Both! Metronome for clean timing and note subdivisions; YouTube 12-bar blues backing tracks for musical expression and groove.
can i mix major and minor pentatonic?
Yes! In blues, sliding between A minor pentatonic (fret 5) and A major pentatonic (fret 2) creates the legendary B.B. King sound.

title: Dynamic programming coin change problem

parts: how does the dynamic programming solution for the Coin Change problem (fewest coins) work?

In the Coin Change problem, given coins `[c1, c2, ...]` and target `amount`, we find minimum coins to make that amount.
Define `dp[i]` as minimum coins needed for amount `i`.
Base case: `dp[0] = 0`, and initialize all other `dp[i] = float('inf')`.
Recurrence relation:
For each amount `i` from 1 to `amount`:
  For each coin `c` in coins:
    if `i >= c`: `dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - c])`.
Return `dp[amount]` if not infinity, else -1.
can you write the python code for this?
what is the time and space complexity?

Time Complexity: $O(A \times C)$ where $A$ is the target amount and $C$ is the number of coin denominations.
Space Complexity: $O(A)$ for the 1D array of size `amount + 1`.
why does a greedy approach fail for coin change?

Greedy picks the largest coin first. Consider coins `[1, 3, 4]` and amount `6`:
- Greedy takes 4, leaving 2, which requires 1 + 1 (total 3 coins: 4, 1, 1).
- Optimal DP solution is 3 + 3 (total 2 coins).
Greedy is only guaranteed optimal for canonical coin systems (like US currency).
how do you modify this to return the actual coins used, not just the count?

Maintain a second array `coin_used = [0] * (amount + 1)`: whenever `1 + dp[i - c] < dp[i]`, set `coin_used[i] = c`. After the loop, backtrack from `curr = amount` appending `coin_used[curr]` and subtracting until `curr == 0`.
what if the problem asks for number of combinations to make the amount?

That's Coin Change II (Unbounded Knapsack)! Swap the loop order: loop over coins on the outer loop, and amounts on the inner loop, with `dp[i] += dp[i - c]`. Outer coin loop ensures combinations are counted without permutation ordering.
can top-down memoization be faster than bottom-up tabulation?

Top-down with `@lru_cache` only computes states that are actually reachable from the target amount, which can be faster if many intermediate amounts are never visited. However, bottom-up avoids recursion call-stack overhead and stack overflows.
what if amount is 0?
`dp[0]` is initialized to 0, which correctly returns 0 coins needed.
how to handle negative coin values?
Standard Coin Change assumes positive integer denominations. Negative coins create potential infinite cycles where you could subtract and add value indefinitely.

title: Circuit breaker tripping and smart plug python script

parts: my bedroom circuit breaker keeps tripping when space heater and computer run together. why?

Standard residential bedroom circuits are 15 amps at 120V (1,800 watts max continuous load $\approx$ 1,440W safe 80% limit). A space heater on high draws 1,500W alone! Adding a gaming PC (300-600W) overloads the circuit, tripping the thermal breaker. Plug the space heater into an outlet on a separate circuit breaker.
makes total sense. i got a smart plug that monitors energy; can i write a python script to poll its wattage every minute?

Yes! Many smart plugs (like TP-Link Kasa) have open Python libraries like `python-kasa`:
```python
import asyncio
from kasa import SmartPlug

async def log_power():
    plug = SmartPlug('192.168.1.50')
    await plug.update()
    print(f'Current Power: {plug.emeter_realtime.power:.1f} W')

asyncio.run(log_power())
```
You can run this in an async loop or cron job logging to SQLite or CSV!

title: Hatchling vs Flit build backends

parts: between hatchling and flit, which is better for a simple open source python library published to PyPI?

Both are modern PEP 517/621 compliant build backends:
- `Flit`: Minimalist, zero-config, ultra-fast. Best if your package structure is standard (`src/pkg` or `pkg/`) and has no complex build plugins.
- `Hatchling`: More extensible, supports custom build hooks (e.g. running code generation before packaging), editable installs with file watching, and version management plugins.
For simple pure-Python libraries, Flit is delightfully lightweight.

title: HSA triple tax advantage stealth IRA

An HSA (Health Savings Account) has three distinct tax advantages:
1. Pre-tax contributions: Deducted from paycheck, avoiding federal, state, and FICA payroll taxes.

title: Zone 2 cardio heart rate calculation

parts: how do i calculate my Zone 2 cardio heart rate for aerobic endurance base building?

Two common methods:
1. Maffetone 180 Formula: $180 - \text{age}$. For a 30-year-old, $180 - 30 = 150\text{ bpm}$. Keep heart rate between 140 and 150 bpm.
2. Percent of Max Heart Rate: 60% to 70% of max heart rate ($220 - \text{age}$). For age 30 (max ~190): Zone 2 is 114 to 133 bpm.
